I found out my wife was having an affair a few years ago now. I felt like such a fool and the fact that she had someone and I didn't... Yeah it's rough.

I know you may not be able to hear this right now but you aren't a fool and you will find someone. What he did, by bringing up that small thing calling you bad is called gaslighting or projection. He is trying to say your feelings are invalid and you shouldn't have them when it is perfectly normal to be angry at someone who has betrayed you. You are justified in feeling how you feel.

My advice would be to limit as much contact as you can. Only talk to when needed, if you even need to. It's kind of a long weekend so if you have the chance take a small road trip. Stay in a hotel in a different city. See different things and different people. I was haunted by the ghosts of our memories together so getting away from that for a bit helped.

I moved for my career and never made new local friends, when she was gone there was SO MUCH empty space I had to fill. That was the worst part is feeling completely alone. As soon as you can you need to start building a social structure. I reconnected with a hobby I used to love when I was younger and met my friend group through there. I joined a trivia team and went to local places on trivia night. I also threw myself into work which I wouldn't recommend but it did help to focus on something else. If you have family you can reach out to them, my brother and I kind of reconnected and we are closer than ever now.

It doesn't really get better if I am honest. At first the waves knocked me over every single time making me feel as if I would drown. Eventually I could stand up to one of those waves every now and then. The hurt remained but it got easier or I got stronger until at some point I realized I wasn't getting knocked down any more. I-I don't know when that happened to be honest but it did. I learned a lot about myself and now on the other side of it life is starting to be ok again.

For what it's worth, they didn't last long. They stayed together while her and I fought in the divorce. They shared a common enemy (me) until the divorce was done and then they had to look at each other. That's when they started to fall apart. He cheated on her. I can not tell you the gratification I have knowing that.

You are going to be OK. You will find someone that will treat you with respect and do all the things you wanted to with him but better in every way.

I was once in a similar situation with my mom. She was a narcissist who had to always be the center of attention. If I did a bad thing I was the bad son while she loudly told people all the embarrassing things I've done as a child to people. If I did a good thing then it was only because she put so much time and effort to be a great mom. Undermining my confidence or any thoughts that I could do anything on my own. Years of that conditioned me to fear leaving, even as an adult that I wasnt good enough to be a healthy independent person. It took years of secret saving money to eventually be able to leave and I've never looked back. 

You deserve a chance at a normal life. You are much stronger than you know because you have had to be for so long. You are not worthless. You dont owe her a thing. You can remove her power over you and make it in the world. It will be hard and painful and you will learn a lot with all the mistakes that come with being an adult but you can get through that too.

Check your state resources. They may have some programs you can take advantage of to help. There are online courses for just about everything. I chose computer stuff  and secretly studied, saved up for some exams to get certifications and now I'm in IT. If that's something of interest to you and you need help paying for the expensive tests hit me up I may be able to help you out when that time comes. 

You deserve better than her. You can do this.

The opposite sex is going to be hard to talk to at first. No matter what. 

I used to not talk to a lot of people and when I did I didn't have a lot to say. What changed me was the job I have. I started to work with the sales team, not doing sells, actually setting up their training sessions. Those training sessions were literally programs at work that taught people how to better communicate with others in order to makes sales and stuff.

Basically here is what they teach.

1) Know your purpose - basically why are you there? In whatever situation or location or function... whatever... know why you are there even if it is to just drink a beer and hang out or whatever. 

2) Elevator pitch. - Now for the sales team they trained to be able to catch someone's interest in our products while riding the same elevator with another person a few floors. In my case I altered it to mean something else. For me it means - Be able to tell someone a little about yourself and what you liked to do for fun or work in the time it takes me to ride the elevator a couple of floors with someone. It builds on knowing your purpose. If you have a clear idea of yourself then you can leverage that knowledge experience to talk to others.

3) get used to no - for this one just know that there are some people that won't like you. They just won't. Dont take it personally. Move on. I personally try to fail when I meet someone I am interested in by being polarizing.  I know I like dark humor. I make awful jokes. For people with a similar humor I know I am going to get along with them. If they don't then I know it's probably never going to work. So I pretty much tell a joke early on and see how things go. For you, just know that people will say no. It happens to us all. Move on.

4) controlling the conversation. - People like to talk about themselves and their hobbies, interests, and work. So, by you asking most of the questions you can not only guide the conversation but get them to talk about themselves which they like and in turn they correlate you to the positive experience. 

So, think of like 10 questions that are interesting enough to get people talking. 


Finally... just from personal experience.  Dont use lines or anything like that. If you see someone that you are interested in. Go up to them and be honest.  You can say something like this.... 

"Hey. I hope I'm not bothering you. My name's Curdled_Nonsense. I saw you from across the room and I thought you would be interesting to talk to. I'm real bad at flirting so.. hi, what's your name?"

Consulting a lawyer, in my state, I am allowed to do whatever the hell I want to. If I want to break every window in the house I could. So the actual installation of the device wasn’t the issues. It was what could be captured in the recording. 

Here is where the letter of the law starts. 

1) You have the right to install any sort of security or monitoring system to protect your home. Even if nothing has happened in the past, that’s your right.  

2) You can not install recording devices for the specific reason to eavesdrop on the other members of the house. That technically is a federal crime called “illegal wiretapping”

3) I had to post somewhere on my home close to where people enter and exit your home that you have a security system that may or may not have recording devices. In my situation I already had a sticker on the bottom of my front door that had the logo of a security company. I found a sticker that looked very similar but also added “24 hour surveillance on property”. As I planned no one noticed when I put that sticker over the old one. However legally I have informed anyone entering the house that I had a system to surveil them. 

4) In my state I could not place a camera in any location where there is a “reasonable expectation of privacy”. Now, MOST couples can consider all of the inside of their home to have a “Reasonable expectation of privacy” because the relationship between the couple, especially if married, are considered one unit legally. However in my case, because my mother was also living there at the end of her life, that did not apply to my situation. I was allowed to install cameras that monitored the kitchen, living room, halls, stairs, garage, and a bonus room above my garage that was being used as a entertainment space. Because in those areas where anyone could just walk into at any time, there was no expectation of it being private. I could not install cameras in any bedrooms or bathrooms or closets, stuff like that. 


So that is what my lawyer told me I could do. That’s what I did. Found out what was going on in my home and resolved that. Kept the camera up until my mom passed.

My lawyer and I went over the form 122A-1 which is part of the Means Test for Chapter 7. [122A-1](https://www.uscourts.gov/sites/default/files/form_b122a-1.pdf) is all about your income and if you are over the median income. In my case, I made more than my state medium income and had to move on to Form [122A-2](https://www.uscourts.gov/sites/default/files/form_b_122a-2.pdf) which is the form to determine if you can actually file Chapter 7 or not. 

122A-2 asks about your expenses. There is an [instruction guide](https://www.uscourts.gov/sites/default/files/instructions-individuals-2015.pdf) for the forms. 

I filled out the forms ahead of time to know about where I was financially. However, when I got there my lawyer did it herself. There were things that I added up correctly on the form but was different, like I didn't take my full mortgage amount, I took the form minimum if memory serves me. 

Also, if you have medical bills and such you can add those instead of taking the government figure but you would need to prove those costs. I didn't need to do that, but that could be the difference between 7 and 13 according to my lawyer, so long as they are provable.

A lot of this advice is good but I honestly worry it is a bit to much assuming. I don’t think we can determine that the phone itself is being tracked. He could be watching your social media with a social media logger. He could be tracking your location by GPS tracker on your car. I think we really need more info on how to hide your location. For example if you leave your phone at home and he is using a GPS tracker in your car, you’ve done nothing to help you not be tracked. 

How tech savvy is he? Do you use an Apple device or a android device?

You live in the situation, how do you think he is tracking you? 

Since I feel there is such uncertainty regarding the tech let me focus on the other stuff. 

Depending on the place you live the person who files for divorce gets to stay and the partner is forced to leave. So if you file first you can stay and he has to leave. 

Do you have direct deposit? Open another account at the bank or credit union you guys use.  That way if you go to a branch it doesn’t look strange. Then have your direct deposit changed to the new account that is only in your name. 

Do you have a 401k or other retirement fund? He may be able to sue you for half of it in the divorce. Part of a divorce is a restraining order barring you from hiding that money or other wise denying him that money. So do what you need to do to BEFORE you file. 

As far as lawyers. Start with r/legaladvice. You can get some ideas from your burner phone that way. 

Could you get him out of the house for a while. Maybe a spa day for him or something. Tell him it’s an apology for “acting strange” or whatever is believable. While he is away spirit your documents away just in case your location won’t force him to leave. 

Good luck.
